C1.quote: In Python, variables are simply names that refer to objects. Variables do not need to be declared before they are assigned and they can even change type in the middle of a program.
C1.statement: Python is dynamically typed: the compiler ignores declarations and all type checking happens at run time, a deliberate corner-cutting simplification that stays safe because every type error is still caught before the interpreter can malfunction.

C2.quote: Python simply drops the compile-time type checking completely. This is entirely in line with Python’s “corner-cutting” philosophy as it’s a simplification of the implementation that does not affect the eventual safety, since all type errors are caught at run time
C2.statement: Prefer the simplest possible implementation and let features fall out of it rather than be specially designed in, cutting corners wherever the gap to a fuller design is small.

C3.quote: In Python, all objects that can be named are said to be "first class."
C3.statement: Everything nameable in Python (functions, classes, methods, modules, types, even the type structure itself) is a first-class, introspectable object that can be passed around, stored, and inspected at run time.

C4.quote: For error handling, Python uses (non-resumable) exceptions.
C4.statement: Errors are handled through exceptions and no operation ever returns a silently undefined value: when no correct result can be computed, an exception is raised rather than letting a bad value pass.

C5.quote: instead of using braces for statement grouping, it uses indentation
C5.statement: Syntax should be clean and human-readable, using indentation (with a clarifying colon) for grouping instead of braces, so program text looks neat and suggests its meaning.

C6.quote: This is one area where Python violated the ABC-inspired philosophy of not requiring users to care about a uninteresting implementation details.
C6.statement: Don't make users care about uninteresting implementation details: unify related concepts (sequences, numbers, statements) into a single general mechanism that behaves consistently.
